original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Two equal-volume N-coordinate lanes with canonical normalized native operators C_p tensor I_(N/2^p) and C_q^(epsilon) tensor I_(N/2^q), 1<=p<q; arbitrary invertible reciprocal encoding, one phased native child i^u C_d tensor I_t with positive integers d>=1 and t>=1, and any restored dirty identity padding. Width-zero scalar children are outside this declared contract. Original endpoint chart wrappers remain fixed outside this contract.
scope_change_reason: Investigate the missing physical-child implication in PR1836's rank-sum screen, rather than claiming an admitted 5% decoder. PR1920 has closed equal-width reciprocal encoding; unequal widths introduce new signed spectral cancellations and need a complete classification, not a larger numerical sweep.
bottleneck_link: Classify exactly when the heterogeneous direct sum is similar to one child; independently bind the consequences to all 215 unequal-rank single-ADD pairs within PR1836's 359 claimed pairs. Establish exact positive opposite-sign exceptions and price their active volume.
stop_rule: Complete the quantified classification, three exact attaining witnesses and all pinned source pairs. Stop synthesis when the complete inherited volume tariff rejects every allowed one-child realization; do not infer unrestricted impossibility.
evidence: README.md proves the all-width unequal signed classification. RESULT.json records 747264 exact spectral trials, 48 matching families through width64, 68 independent cyclic/binomial spectrum checks, 215 heterogeneous source gates in both orientations, three full rational encoding witnesses (2304 matrix entries), nine controls plus six matrix mutation witnesses, and certified counterfactual profile brackets. No admitted replacement profile or new kappa.
author: Adam Gall (@adamgall), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in research, mathematics, implementation, verification and writing. No human or proof-assistant review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can independent nonreciprocal entry/exit adapters realize a heterogeneous joint child with a complete cost below separate calls?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Such adapters are outside the reciprocal packing contract; a new inexpensive interface could bypass this spectral obstruction.
open_questions.first_step: Specify the exact two-lane source and output charts for one (1,2) selected gate and exhibit the adapter matrices with full copied volume, inverse/restoration and native costs.
open_questions.blocked_by: No inexpensive physical nonreciprocal adapter or alternative child tariff is established here.

optimistic_budget: Retain PR1836's full profile screen as a conditional planning target. Every alleged one-child realization must preserve full lane volume; square trace forces active child volume2N. Any positive unequal-width exception has d=max(p,q)+2, hence inherited child expression2 A V d^sigma exceeds A V(p^sigma+q^sigma) for0<sigma<1, even granting encoding, scalar gate, phases, copies, frames, hosting, restoration and precision free. This compares available upper-bound expressions, not optimal runtime.
method_and_domain: Written Gaussian-integer valuation and four-trace argument for all positive unequal p,q; exact binomial and cyclic-recursion spectral checks through width64, rational Walsh basis witnesses, independently reconstructed source-event census with frame/rational-shear checks. All positive unequal p,q for theorem; finite spectra 1<=p<q<=64 and d through q+3, both signs, four phases; source all A/B/tail gates in both selected emitted orientations; explicit witness p=1,q=2,d=4,N=8 and p=2,q=3,d=5,N=16.

overlap.limits: Cached metadata, local READMEs/TASK/ledger including merged work, and targeted live source reads; not arbitrary diffs or a novelty certificate. PR1920 equal-width classification and PR1924 clean encodings are explicitly credited. PR1866 is an unrelated bilinear rank-six tensor, not a Clifford operator reciprocal encoding.
